qs.q: A severely injured pedestrian undergoes massive transfusion protocol initiation following a severe pelvic crush injury. Thromboelastography (TEG) returns a prolonged R-time and a decreased maximum amplitude (MA). Which specific therapeutic intervention is best indicated by these combined parameters?
o: Infusing concentrated factor complexes alongside fresh frozen plasma
Administering pooled platelet concentrates together with plasma fractions
Supplementing recombinant factor VIIa alongside standard cryoprecipitate
Giving synthetic antifibrinolytic agents prior to definitive surgery
Starting continuous calcium chloride infusions alongside packed cells
qs.e: Prolonged R-time indicates clotting factor deficiency, while low maximum amplitude reflects platelet dysfunction requiring concentrates.
qs.s: Weekly Year 4: General Surgery Exam - November 13, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: An emergency room physician evaluates a polytrauma patient whose thromboelastography (TEG) tracing shows normal R-time, normal K-time, normal alpha angle, but a markedly decreased maximum amplitude (MA) with a normal Ly30 value. What is the precise cellular defect indicated by these findings?
o: Impaired polymerization kinetics of soluble monomeric fibrin structures
Severe systemic deficiency of circulating soluble fibrinogen proteins
Accelerated enzymatic breakdown of stabilized cross-linked networks
Delayed initial enzymatic generation of stable thrombin enzyme complexes
Isolated functional impairment or numerical deficit of circulating platelets
qs.e: Maximum amplitude (MA) on TEG specifically reflects platelet strength and function.
qs.s: Weekly Year 4: General Surgery Exam - November 13, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: An emergency physician reviews the thromboelastography (TEG) profile of a bleeding trauma patient and notes a very rapid disappearance of the clot, with the amplitude dropping significantly within 30 minutes of reaching maximum amplitude (high Ly30). Which therapeutic agent should be administered immediately?
o: Platelet concentrates to improve overall clot strength parameters
Fresh frozen plasma to replenish depleted coagulation factor levels
Tranexamic acid to inhibit excessive plasminogen activation pathways
Cryoprecipitate to provide supplemental fibrinogen protein substrates
Prothrombin complex concentrates to restore normal thrombin generation
qs.e: A high Ly30 value indicates hyperfibrinolysis, which is treated with antifibrinolytics like tranexamic acid.
qs.s: Weekly Year 4: General Surgery Exam - November 13, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A trauma patient with a pelvic fracture has a TEG displaying a markedly decreased maximum amplitude (MA) coupled with normal R-time and K-time. What underlying pathological process does this specific viscoelastic profile indicate?
o: Severe functional deficiency of circulating fibrinogen
Reduced platelet aggregation and functional capacity
Excessive systemic activation of endogenous fibrinolysis
Depletion of intrinsic coagulation enzyme complexes
Impaired cross-linking due to factor XIII deficiency
qs.e: Maximum amplitude on thromboelastography directly measures the overall strength of the clot, which is determined primarily by platelet function.
qs.s: Weekly Year 4: General Surgery Exam - November 13, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: In ROTEM terminology, which parameter is analogous to TEG’s maximum amplitude (MA)?
o: Maximum clot firmness (MCF)
Clot formation time (CFT)
Clotting time (CT)
Maximum lysis (ML)
qs.e: Maximum clot firmness (MCF) in ROTEM corresponds to MA in TEG. CT and CFT relate to clot initiation and formation time, while ML measures lysis.
